symptom: Under `mdl 1;` a re-run of `create or modify microflow` fails with "this change cannot be spliced into the stored flow: ... drop return: cannot drop the EndEvent at (x, y)" whenever the body does not spell a trailing `return`, and a changed return value fails with "replace return 7: ... a return inside an inserted fragment is not supported yet". Under mdl 0 the same statements silently took the lossy MDL-V1-REBUILD fallback, so the upgrade property test (MXCLI_UPGRADE_ALL=1) showed header-only scripts writing different models (bug-tests/914, 951, doctype-tests/microflow-document-properties).
cause: The stored side of diff-then-patch is the full-layout describe, which prints the final end event as `@position(x, y) return;`. A declared body that falls through has no such statement, so the LCS saw a stored return the script dropped, and a return-for-return change became a Replace of the EndEvent with a fragment that itself ends the flow. Masked behind that refusal: a run of statements that are stored ones redrawn (all @positions changed, or a new first statement with @start) went through as replace + drops, writing new nodes where the splice places them and losing the stated positions.
insight: The header was not the cause: mdl 1 parses these bodies identically; it only turns the fallback into a refusal, which exposed a diff bug mdl 0 was hiding behind a warned rebuild. An implicit end and a trailing `return` are the same end event, so state the implicit one before diffing; returns at the end of both sides of a run are the same node and a value change is a property edit, not a replace. Removing a refusal can expose the silent path behind it: after fixing the end event, re-run the scripts the refusal used to stop and read what they now write (951 would otherwise have spliced with every stated position ignored).
